anatomy.flutter: glass.dart's `GlassVariant` enum has FOUR members: `panel, navigation, prominent, control`. `GlassVariant.navigation` builds `_GlassPanelClear`, documented as 'A clearer card-scale glass panel for floating navigation chrome ... Only the foundation-owned fill opacity is lower [_clearPanelFill / SurfaceOpacity.navigationGlass], so content moving beneath remains visibly present through the blur.'
anatomy.web: Grepping styles/utilities.css finds exactly three `@utility` blocks: `glass-panel` (L71), `glass-panel-deep` (L109), `glass-control` (L120) — no `glass-navigation` or `glass-panel-navigation` utility exists anywhere in the file. styles/tokens.css has no `navigation-glass`/`navigationGlass` opacity token either. The glass doc page's own Classes section lists only these same three: 'glass-panel', 'glass-panel-deep', 'glass-control'.
anatomy.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: Flutter's `GlassVariant.navigation` (a fourth, clearer-fill glass variant 'for floating navigation chrome') has NO corresponding web CSS utility or doc entry at all — confirmed by grep of styles/utilities.css and styles/tokens.css (2026-09-11), which surface only the three utilities glass.dart's own header comment says exist ('Three utilities, one material'). Either the web is missing a fourth utility Flutter already ships, or Flutter ships a variant that was never given a CSS home. File/line: lib/src/components/ui/glass.dart:494-556 (GlassVariant enum, `navigation` case) and :607-649 (_GlassPanelClear); styles/utilities.css:71-141 (only glass-panel/glass-panel-deep/glass-control declared).

api.flutter: Glass({variant = GlassVariant.panel, required radius, padding, required child}); glass.dart's own header comment enumerates the three CSS-backed recipes precisely: `glass-panel` ('Translucent --card, a backdrop blur, a hairline rim ... and --shadow-e2 beneath'), `glass-panel-deep` ('byte-identical to glass-panel except its ambient layer is --shadow-e4'), `glass-control` ('A --foreground wash and two inset layers, and nothing else: no blur, no saturate, no ambient shadow').
api.web: glass doc page Classes block: glass-panel = 'backdrop-blur-xl backdrop-saturate-150, a card-coloured fill ... a --rim-strong top highlight and a foreground-tinted hairline rim, at --shadow-e2'; glass-panel-deep = 'Identical fill and rim to glass-panel, at --shadow-e4 instead of e2'; glass-control = 'No blur, no ambient shadow ... sized for a 40-56px control.'

states.flutter: Glass/_GlassPanel/_GlassPanelDeep/_GlassControl are all StatelessWidget with no hover/focus/pressed logic — pure static paint (fill + backdrop filter + inset shadow layers).
states.web: The glass doc page's Reduced Motion section states outright: 'Not applicable. None of the three classes animate — the blur, fill and rim are static declarations,' and there is no hover:/focus-visible: rule anywhere in the glass-panel/glass-panel-deep/glass-control blocks of utilities.css.
states.note: Both platforms declare glass a purely static material with no interaction states of its own — matches the effects-family pattern (a class/utility, not a control), so states genuinely do not apply on either side.

disabled.flutter: No `enabled`/disabled parameter exists on Glass or any of its private variant widgets in glass.dart.
disabled.web: None of glass-panel/glass-panel-deep/glass-control in utilities.css declare a disabled or data-disabled rule.
disabled.note: Glass is a material class applied to a host surface, not a control — a disabled state belongs to whatever interactive element (if any) is placed inside a glass panel, not to the material itself, on either platform.

interaction.flutter: glass.dart mounts no GestureDetector, MouseRegion or FocusNode anywhere — Glass is pure paint via Stack/ClipRRect/BackdropFilter/CustomPaint.
interaction.web: None of the three utilities declare any pointer/keyboard-driven rule; the class only sets background-color, box-shadow and (for panel variants) backdrop-filter.
interaction.note: Glass carries no interaction of its own on either platform — it is a background material a host wears, with the host owning any interactivity.

semantics.flutter: No Semantics widget appears anywhere in glass.dart; Glass paints purely visual layers around [child] and forwards the child's own semantics unchanged.
semantics.web: utilities.css's glass-* utilities set no ARIA attributes; the glass doc page's Accessibility section only warns about contrast ('measure the rendered pixel, not the token'), naming no role/label concern.
semantics.note: Glass contributes no accessibility semantics of its own on either platform — the doc page's only accessibility guidance is a contrast warning about the translucent fill, which is content-authoring advice rather than a semantics contract, so n/a applies to both sides equally.
